_readme: Card fields: max ~25 words each. Facts only from CLAUDE.md 'Facts' or the linked NASA page. Unknown = TODO_VERIFY. coordsVerified=false means lat/lon still need a teammate check.

machines.name: Viking 1 Lander
machines.why: To photograph Mars up close and test its soil for signs of life.
machines.howItWorked: A small robot arm scooped soil into onboard labs that looked for signs of living things.
machines.found: The first US pictures from the surface of Mars. Its life tests were not taken as proof of life.
machines.status: Mission ended in November 1982. The lander is still at Chryse Planitia.
log: Chryse Planitia. I touched down on July 20, 1976.
I took the first US pictures from the ground on Mars.
My arm scooped red soil into my little labs. Was anything alive in it?
machines.numanNote: The Numans call this one 'the first to knock on the door.'
machines.teaser: This lander searched the soil for life.

hotspots.label: Scooped soil for the biology labs. TODO_VERIFY position
Took the first US photos from the Martian surface. TODO_VERIFY position

machines.name: Opportunity rover
machines.why: To look for rocks and soil that show whether Mars once had water.
machines.howItWorked: Six wheels, solar panels for power, and a robot arm with tools to study rocks up close.
machines.found: Evidence that Mars was once wet, including small round hematite grains called 'blueberries'.
machines.status: Last heard from June 10, 2018, during a dust storm. Mission declared over in February 2019.
log: Meridiani Planum. They planned for 90 days.
I drove about 28 miles over almost 15 years.
I found signs that Mars was once wet.
In 2018 a dust storm covered the Sun, and I never woke up.
machines.numanNote: The Numans say dust storms still sing its name.
machines.teaser: Built for 90 days. Lasted almost 15 years.

machines.name: InSight lander
machines.why: To study the deep inside of Mars.
machines.howItWorked: A seismometer sat on the ground under a dome that blocked wind and heat, listening for shaking.
machines.found: More than 1,300 marsquakes. The biggest was about magnitude 5 in May 2022.
machines.status: Dust covered its solar panels. NASA ended the mission in December 2022.
log: Elysium Planitia. I landed in November 2018.
I set my seismometer on the ground under a dome. Then I listened.
Dust slowly covered my solar panels, and in December 2022 I went quiet.
machines.numanNote: The Numans tune their songs to the rhythm of marsquakes.

machines.name: Ingenuity helicopter
machines.why: To test whether a helicopter could fly in the thin air of Mars.
machines.howItWorked: Two rotors spin in opposite directions, very fast, to grip the thin Martian air.
machines.found: The first powered, controlled flight on another planet, on April 19, 2021. It flew 72 times.
machines.status: Rotor damage ended its mission in January 2024. It still rests in Jezero Crater.
log: Jezero Crater. I rode to Mars under Perseverance.
On April 19, 2021, I lifted off. No one had flown on another planet before.
I carry a tiny piece of fabric from the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer.
machines.numanNote: The Numans had never seen a machine dance in the air before.
machines.teaser: The first aircraft to fly on another planet.
